summary:
CropWise AI is an AI-powered, climate-resilient agricultural decision-support platform developed by Team Black Mamba for the challenge *Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.

The platform combines NASA Earth observation data, historical climate and soil information, geospatial analysis, statistical modeling, and IoT-based ground observations to help farmers better understand changing environmental conditions. It analyzes key indicators such as temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, vegetation health (NDVI), and water deficit to identify potential agricultural risks and support informed farming decisions.

CropWise AI also features Data Fusion and Validation to compare satellite observations with local ESP32 sensor readings, alongside Statistical Intelligence techniques such as correlation analysis, regression, PCA, and clustering to uncover environmental patterns.

By transforming complex Earth observation data into accessible, practical insights, CropWise AI aims to help farmers adapt to changing conditions, improve agricultural planning, and build more resilient farming communities.
details:
Project Details — CropWise AI

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

CropWise AI is an AI-powered agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers understand environmental changes and make more informed farming decisions. It addresses the challenge of adapting agriculture to shifting climate conditions by combining NASA Earth observation data, historical environmental records, geospatial analysis, statistical intelligence, and IoT-based ground observations.

The platform analyzes important agricultural indicators, including surface temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, vegetation health (NDVI), evapotranspiration, and water deficit. Farmers can explore environmental conditions through interactive visualizations and location-based analysis.

Its Data Fusion and Validation system compares satellite-derived information with local observations collected through an ESP32-based IoT device. The Statistical Intelligence engine applies descriptive statistics, Pearson and Spearman correlation, multiple linear regression, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and K-Means clustering to identify environmental relationships, patterns, and potential agricultural vulnerabilities.

These insights support climate analysis, crop planning, environmental risk assessment, and crop rotation decisions.

2. Benefits and intended impact

CropWise AI aims to make complex satellite and environmental information understandable and useful for farmers. Its intended benefits include:

  • Helping farmers understand local climate and environmental conditions.
  • Identifying potential heat stress, water shortages, and soil moisture problems.
  • Supporting better crop selection, planting, and crop rotation decisions.
  • Connecting large-scale satellite observations with local ground-level sensor readings.
  • Encouraging data-driven and climate-resilient agricultural practices.
  • Making advanced Earth observation technology more accessible to farming communities.

Our long-term vision is to help farmers become better prepared for unpredictable environmental conditions while supporting sustainable agricultural productivity.

3. Tools, technologies, and hardware

Data sources and Earth observation:

  • NASA POWER — meteorological and solar radiation information.
  • NASA GPM/IMERG — precipitation observations.
  • NASA SMAP — soil moisture observations.
  • MODIS — vegetation indices and evapotranspiration.
  • Landsat 8/9 — land-surface and vegetation analysis.
  • ECOSTRESS — land-surface temperature.
  • SoilGrids — soil properties and composition.
  • NASADEM — elevation and terrain information.
  • GEDI — forest structure and biomass observations.

Software and development technologies:

  • Next.js and React — web application and user interface.
  • TypeScript/JavaScript — application development.
  • Python — statistical and data analysis workflows.
  • Neon PostgreSQL — environmental and application data storage.
  • Google Maps Platform — geospatial visualization.
  • TanStack Query — client-side data fetching and caching.
  • AI and machine learning techniques — environmental analysis and decision support.

IoT hardware:

  • ESP32 development board.
  • DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor.
  • Capacitive soil moisture sensor.
  • Analog rain sensor.
  • GPS module for location-based observations.

4. What makes CropWise AI creative?

The creativity of CropWise AI comes from bringing together several technologies that are often used separately. Instead of simply displaying satellite data, it combines Earth observation, local IoT measurements, statistical modeling, geospatial intelligence, and AI-assisted interpretation in one agricultural platform.

Its Data Fusion system provides a way to compare satellite observations with local sensor measurements, while Statistical Intelligence evaluates multiple analytical methods rather than relying on a single model. This combination helps transform environmental measurements into understandable agricultural insights.

5. Factors considered during development

Our team considered farmer accessibility, changing climate conditions, environmental data quality, spatial and temporal resolution, sensor calibration, measurement uncertainty, and the practical limitations of satellite observations.

We also considered the differences between satellite-scale measurements and individual farm-level conditions. Our goal is not to replace farmers' experience, but to provide additional scientific evidence and accessible information that can support their decisions.
